Description: Reasoning told in every language Lambek reads (fr, en, de, es, nl, pt, it), the same conversations in each: all and no, a thing that is or does, with what it does to, a chain of two, the fact told first, and what cannot be concluded (a thing never told of, all read the other way, some, a thing told of another); and, since version 1.1, a thing told not to be, who is, what all are like, two told at once, no read through a chain and the other way, no with what it does to. Each case is a conversation of its own, measured as bench/messages.json is (Invoke-LambekMessageBenchmark). The calibration split and the test split say the same kinds of things with other words; the test split is frozen: TestHash is the hash of its cases, never edit them while working on Lambek (version 1.1 added cases to both splits, before Lambek was worked on with them; version 1.2 added a question asked of he, il, er, hij (and the pronoun said where the language may leave it out: el, ele, lui), two things told in one message, and a pronoun told after its name in the same message, to both splits, written after Lambek was taught to read them: the test split of 1.2 was not blind, and is frozen from now; version 1.3 added a kind said with what those of it do, after a relative pronoun, and the same rule about one never said to do it, to both splits, written before they were run; version 1.4 added two kinds said the same at once, and two things said of one kind at once, joined by the word that says both, to both splits, written before they were run; version 1.5 added one said to be more than another, twice, and asked of the first and the last either way, to both splits, written before they were run; version 1.6 added two said at once to be more than a third, and one said to be so, or not, with one more so than another, to both splits, written before they were run; version 1.7 added one said to be one of two kinds and not the one, what holds of both kinds, a rule saying one of two and not the one, and one of two asked of the first alone, to both splits, written before they were run). Written by hand, never learned from.
